name: Deep ITM Long Put (short-stock replacement)
summary: Buy a -0.80 to -0.90 delta put as a defined-risk substitute for shorting 100 shares, with no borrow fee and no unlimited upside risk.
max_profit: (strike - 0) x 100 - debit if the underlying goes to zero; tracks the short nearly 1:1 below the strike
max_loss: Debit x 100 - the key advantage over shorting stock, where losses are unlimited.

greeks.theta: small negative - only the thin extrinsic decays

when_to_use: When you want short exposure without borrow cost, hard-to-borrow risk or unlimited upside. Especially valuable on hard-to-borrow names, though that borrow cost is embedded in the put's price.
entry_rules: Extrinsic value = put mid - max(0, strike - spot); require extrinsic <= 2.5% of strike
Check the put-call parity implied borrow rate: if the embedded borrow exceeds 15% annualised, the synthetic short is priced against you - skip
management_rules: Manage like a short stock position: hold while price is below the 50 EMA
Roll out when DTE < 45 into the same delta 90+ days out, as a single net order
Stop at -35% of debit or a daily close above the 50 EMA
Take partial profit at +50% of debit; trail the remainder 1.5 ATR above price
exit_rules: Sell to close on the stop, the trend break, or at 45 DTE

Never carry into expiration week. An ITM put at expiry auto-exercises into SHORT 100 shares, an uncovered short equity position with unlimited risk and potential buy-in. Hard flatten/roll 5 trading days before expiry
assignment_risk: None (long). Auto-exercise into short stock is the critical hazard and the single worst unintended outcome available in this family.
buying_power: Debit only - no short-stock margin, no borrow.
liquidity_needs: Deep ITM put markets are wide. Reject above 3% of mid.
common_mistakes: Ignoring the embedded borrow cost in hard-to-borrow names; letting it expire ITM and inheriting a short equity position.
